record.context_brief: Closed geodesics in fluid configuration space
record.original_question: If M is a compact surface of genus at least 2, or a multiconnected bounded domain in R^2 with at least two holes, does D_mu^s(M) contain a closed geodesic for the L2 hydrodynamic metric?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be either a compact orientable surface (without boundary) of genus $g \geq 2$ equipped with a smooth area form $\mu$, or a bounded multiply-connected domain in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with at least two holes equipped with the standard area form. For $s > \dim(M)/2 + 1$, let $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ denote the group of Sobolev-class $H^s$ diffeomorphisms of $M$ that preserve the area form $\mu$ (and, in the boundary case, that fix the boundary or preserve it appropriately). Equip $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ with the right-invariant $L^2$ (hydrodynamic) Riemannian metric, whose geodesic equation on $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ corresponds to the incompressible Euler equation for an ideal fluid on $M$.

Question: Does $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ admit a closed (i.e., nonconstant periodic) geodesic with respect to this $L^2$ metric?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of existence of closed geodesics in the $L^2$ hydrodynamic metric on volume-preserving diffeomorphism groups of higher-genus surfaces or multiply-connected planar domains is a known open problem in geometric hydrodynamics. Related results (e.g. non-self-intersection of geodesics by Drivas and collaborators) constrain the structure of such geodesics but do not establish existence. No source found that resolves the existence question in these cases.

status_evidence.title: Geodesics on group of measure preserving diffeomorphisms do not self-intersect
status_evidence.snippet: For surfaces of any genus, geodesics in D_μ(M) are either injective or periodic.
status_evidence.claim: Related work addresses structural properties of geodesics but does not establish existence of closed geodesics in the cases asked.

status_evidence.title: Volume-Preserving Diffeomorphism Groups
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of geometry of volume-preserving diffeomorphism groups with L2 metric.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of closed geodesics on D_μ^s(M) for higher genus surfaces or multiconnected domains remains an open question.
